files.purpose: UpdateChecker is the app-layer MainActor @Observable singleton that polls Droppy's public GitLab releases API for a newer stable build shipping a .dmg, keeping the newest qualifying release plus a persisted lastCheckedAt/lastError so the About page can show a known update the instant it opens. It also owns the small AppVersion value type used to compare the running build against whatever the feed reports, and the AvailableUpdate/GitLabRelease Codable models that carry the release's version, tag, download URL, size, notes and page URL through persistence and into the UI.
calls_into: URLSession (ephemeral session with fixed timeouts and User-Agent)
side_effects: One HTTPS GET per check to gitlab.com's public releases API (no auth token)
One HTTPS HEAD per check when the chosen release's size is unknown
Writes UserDefaults keys updateChecker_release, updateChecker_lastChecked, updateChecker_notifiedVersion
Posts at most one local UNNotificationRequest per new version on a background check that finds an update, requesting notification authorization the first time if not yet determined
Registers (and never unregisters) an NSApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification observer and a long-lived background Task while startBackgroundChecks() has not returned early
platform_assumptions: AppKit + UserNotifications for the local update-available banner
persisted_fields: updateChecker_notifiedVersion -> String (last version a notification was posted for)
feature_notes: The only functional line touched between B2 and B3 is the startBackgroundChecks() guard at (B2) line 133: 'guard backgroundTask == nil, !WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, !AppInfo.isDevelopment else { return }' became 'guard backgroundTask == nil, !CaptureRun.isEnabled, !AppInfo.isDevelopment else { return }'. This is a pure call-site rename, not a new capability: in B2, App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift already forwarded its own isEnabled (and outputDirectory/isTourRun/storageRoot/defaults) straight through to Core/Support/CaptureRun.swift ('nonisolated static var isEnabled: Bool { CaptureRun.isEnabled }'), and the B2->B3 diff of WebsiteCaptures.swift (git diff 1fbf81e6..HEAD -- DroppyCode/App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift) shows exactly those five forwarding properties deleted and every internal call site (log(), prepare(), run()) switched to call CaptureRun directly. UpdateChecker.swift:133 was updated to match that same App-layer cleanup: CaptureRun.isEnabled resolves to the identical boolean (true only when the process was launched with --website-captures or --tour-captures) both before and after, so startBackgroundChecks()'s observable behaviour (whether the launch/6-hourly/activation-triggered background check schedule starts) is unchanged. This is a refactor_no_observable_change for UpdateChecker.swift itself, with churn 2 (one line removed, one added) matching the inventory's reported churn.

No other hunk touches this file between B2 and B3; the AppVersion parsing/comparison, AvailableUpdate/GitLabRelease models, the fixed GitLab API endpoint and User-Agent, the check()/fetchReleases()/newestRelease()/downloadSize()/persist()/notifyOnce() logic, and the disk-image asset filter are byte-identical to B2.
